key_insight: Pressure-tuned LaMoN$_3$ stays dynamically stable up to 40 GPa while its bandgap, exciton binding energy, and nonlinear optical response can be optimized to improve photovoltaic performance.
engineering_relevance: The study identifies pressure windows for designing ferroelectric nitride absorbers that balance linear absorption and nonlinear shift-current generation, supporting next-generation multi-junction solar device concepts.
method: First-principles DFT and DFPT for structural, electronic, and vibrational stability
Many-body perturbation theory (G$_0$W$_0$ and BSE) for quasiparticle gaps and excitons
Tight-binding modeling to analyze optical response trends under pressure
evidence_signal: Across 0–40 GPa, the G$_0$W$_0$ bandgap drops from 2.17 eV to 1.45 eV, SLME increases, exciton binding energy decreases, and the bulk photovoltaic/shift-current response peaks near 15 GPa.
watch_item: The results are computational predictions only, so practical implementation depends on whether the required high-pressure phases and device architectures can be experimentally realized and retained.
paper_title: Harnessing Linear and Nonlinear Optical Responses in Ferroelectric LaMoN$_3$ for Enhanced Photovoltaic Efficiency
